score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 7 major vendors (BizProspex, CampaignLake, MedicoReach, InfoGlobalData, AverickMedia, HealthcareMailing, BookYourData) currently selling pharmacist email lists ranging from 27K to 171K+ records with pricing starting at $200+ (BookYourData offers 40,982 contacts, implying per-contact costs similar to other healthcare professional lists at $0.10-$0.40/contact). Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) pharmaceutical manufacturers and wholesalers (Pfizer, McKesson, AmerisourceBergen, Cardinal Health) marketing prescription drugs, generics, and specialty medications to retail and hospital pharmacists — each pharmacist influences $500K-$5M/year in medication dispensing decisions; (2) pharmacy technology and management software vendors (PioneerRx, QS/1, PrimeRx, BestRx, Liberty Software) selling $300-$2,000/month SaaS subscriptions for pharmacy management systems (PMS), inventory control, e-prescribing, and patient management; (3) pharmacy equipment and automation suppliers (Parata, ScriptPro, Omnicell, BD Rowa) selling automated dispensing systems, pill counters, packaging machines, and robotics at $50K-$500K per pharmacy setup; and (4) pharmacy continuing education (CE) providers (ACPE-accredited platforms, pharmacy associations, CPE Monitor) marketing mandatory CE courses — all pharmacists must complete 15-30 hours of CE every 1-2 years (state-dependent) to maintain licensure at $200-$600/year spend per pharmacist. All 50 states maintain public pharmacist license registries via their State Boards of Pharmacy, accessible through state-specific pharmacy board websites with data including pharmacist name, license number, status (active/inactive), issue/renewal dates, and practice location. Zero PII — all professional credential data. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state pharmacy boards (Texas offers database access updated M-F by noon, multiple states have lookup tools), deduplicate multi-state license holders, normalize practice affiliations. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($800-$3,000/year) or per-contact pricing, leaving a clear gap for a one-time $79-$99 CSV. Audience size is substantial: approximately 340,000 licensed pharmacists nationwide (BLS data), creating a TAM of 10,000+ potential B2B buyers (pharma companies, software vendors, equipment manufacturers, CE providers). Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed public data availability across all states with established lookup systems, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, clear B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior, and moderate engineering lift.

data_wanted: All 50 state Boards of Pharmacy plus DC maintain public pharmacist license registries, accessible via state-specific pharmacy board websites under names like '[State] Board of Pharmacy' or '[State] Pharmacy Board'. No authentication required for lookup (though some states may require scraping vs. bulk download). Key fields per license: pharmacist full name (first, middle initial, last), license number (format varies by state, typically 6-10 digits or alphanumeric), license status (active, inactive, expired, suspended, revoked), original issue date, current expiration or renewal date, practice type or setting (retail pharmacy, hospital/health system, clinical, specialty, consulting, long-term care, mail-order — availability varies by state), employer name or pharmacy affiliation (where publicly listed; some states list specific pharmacy chains like CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, or hospital systems), practice address city and state (some states list full street address, others only city/state). Target all active and inactive-but-not-revoked licenses (exclude only revoked, surrendered, or disciplinary-suspended). Scope to individual pharmacists only (RPh and PharmD credentials) — exclude pharmacy technicians (which have separate registrations). Approximately 340,000 active pharmacist licenses nationwide as of 2026 per BLS data (note: multi-state license holders mean unique individual count is ~310K-320K). Target output: 340K rows, one per license. Data is 100% public per state pharmacy practice acts (professional licensing records are public information under state Freedom of Information laws). Texas State Board of Pharmacy updates databases Monday through Friday by 12 noon with searchable lookup tool. Multiple states offer similar real-time or daily-updated lookup systems. Some states may offer bulk downloads or API access (requires state-by-state verification).

(3) Pharmacy equipment and automation suppliers: dispensing systems and robotics range $50K-$500K per pharmacy setup; vendors pay $5,000-$15,000/year for pharmacist databases, so a $99 CSV provides 50×-151× cost savings, and a single equipment sale yields 500×-5,000× ROI. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $500 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions $800-$3,000/year or per-contact pricing, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with confirmed public data availability across all 51 jurisdictions creates a clear low-price entry wedge.
